title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Application Close Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback test, RFC 9220 parser/formatter regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted websocket Extended CONNECT tunnel whose application handler reads a masked client data frame, writes an unmasked close frame with status 1003 and reason `unsupported`, and completes the writable side of the stream.
preconditions: The WebSocket frame parser remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0002`.
The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
The accepted tunnel message helper boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0004`.
The ping/pong helper boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0005`.
expected_result: The focused loopback and parser/formatter tests pass, the new RFC 9220 application-close requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 server handler path now has locally verified explicit application close behavior on accepted RFC 9220 tunnels. Evidence class is local same-process loopback over the repository QUIC transport; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
